tldr: One test for fixed binary potential outcomes can compare harm-cap scenarios while retaining validity for every weak-null table. Its target \(A_n(k)\) is the smallest worst additive loss in guaranteed power relative to the distinct known-cap causal oracles. The common count lift, endpoints, exact zero/positive phase and positive stability bound are proved supporting results. Exact twelve-unit certificates refute monotone, endpoint-only and minimal-effect simplifications. The twenty-unit regression test is also proved: every cap value used in that finite test has an independent exact certificate, and deleting one positive-width parent loses exactly its positive oracle-drop source. The all-size interior-oracle selector, positive-regret contact frontier and active-null classification remain open. A finite exact verifier and a safe hybrid do not replace those open questions. Under the broad effect-only alternatives, any achievable guaranteed-power target of at least one half has the same cap-specific and globally valid benchmark, so conventional eighty-percent planning has zero adaptation cost.
gap: Existing robust-testing mixture bounds and exact binary inference methods do not evaluate simultaneous guaranteed-power deficits against cap-specific validity oracles.
fill: An evaluated structural selector must identify the complete contact geometry and certify both its oracle inputs and its all-design optimal value.
